Perfect! Now I have the reference data. According to this:
- Ar-H (aromatic C-H): 115-130 ppm
- Ar-C (aromatic quaternary carbon): 130-150 ppm

Looking at my 13C NMR data again:
- 166.40 ppm - This is in the carboxylic ester range (160-170 ppm), so it's a carbonyl carbon, NOT aromatic
- 131.87 ppm - This is in the Ar-C range (130-150 ppm), so it's aromatic
- 129.70 ppm (×2) - This is in the Ar-H range (115-130 ppm), so these are aromatic (2 carbons)
- 129.01 ppm (×2) - This is in the Ar-H range (115-130 ppm), so these are aromatic (2 carbons)
- 129.00 ppm - This is in the Ar-H range (115-130 ppm), so this is aromatic (1 carbon)
- 52.24 ppm - This is in the H3C-O range (50-60 ppm), likely a methoxy group, NOT aromatic
- 43.47 ppm - Aliphatic, NOT aromatic
- 38.60 ppm - Aliphatic, NOT aromatic

So the aromatic carbons are:
- 131.87 ppm: 1 carbon
- 129.70 ppm: 2 carbons
- 129.01 ppm: 2 carbons
- 129.00 ppm: 1 carbon

Total aromatic carbons = 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 6 carbons
